dedupe_keys.name: simulation based digital twin of cheltenham general and gloucestershire royal hospitals

description: This vendor case study describes a simulation model that Decision Lab built in AnyLogic as the foundation of a digital twin of two English hospitals, Cheltenham General Hospital and Gloucestershire Royal Hospital, run by one NHS Foundation Trust. The model covers 75 units and buildings and simulates the whole journey of elective and emergency patients: discrete-event logic represents hospital processes and agent-based logic represents patients, with specialty wards, cancellation of planned surgery when no bed is free, nurse triage in the emergency department, critical care, priority-scored bed queues and outlier patients placed in wards of another specialty. A manager-facing interface reports performance by hospital, department, location and patient, and results are exported as CSV files for the NHS analytics team. The AnyLogic Company publishes the case study to show hospital digital twins; the trust wanted to understand how bottlenecks in one department ripple through the system when emergency and planned patients compete for beds and staff. Coverage is two hospital sites at the level of individual patients and beds. It is a free public web page; the model itself is not published. Caveats: it is marketing material with no dates, validation results or quantified outcomes for this project, and the software is commercial. Simulation uses: digital twin and capacity planning of hospital operations, including stress tests of winter peaks and planning a new ward, with agent-based patient behaviour. Related: open hospital demand models such as CHIME (catalogued as model-chime) address the same bed-capacity question at regional scale.
